title: Signal-Amplification Strategies for Gold-Nanoparticle Lateral Flow Assays: A Structured Review of Limit-of-Detection Improvement Relative to Conventional GNP-LFA
content: Gold-nanoparticle lateral flow assays (GNP-LFAs) are attractive for point-of-care testing, but their conventional colorimetric readout often limits analytical sensitivity. This structured review asked which signal-amplification strategies produce the greatest improvement in limit of detection (LOD) relative to a conventional GNP-LFA comparator, and by what magnitude. Candidate records were identified through an investigator-directed keyword search and screened at full text by a single reviewer; 29 of 36 assessed records met eligibility, contributing 36 comparator arms across nine mechanism categories. Reported LOD fold-improvements ranged from no measurable gain to 1000x. Enzyme/catalytic (nanozyme) amplification spanned the widest range (4x–1000x across 5 arms), whereas silver/gold enhancement was the most frequently reported category (7 arms, 4 studies), with gains mostly below 40x and one study reporting up to 488x. Two arms showed no meaningful improvement over a conventional or visual-readout comparator. Gains varied substantially within and between categories and were analyte- and format-dependent; same-study and literature-baseline comparators answer different questions and should not be treated interchangeably. The largest gains came from mechanisms acting on detection chemistry rather than flow control or label loading, although most categories rest on few independent studies. Single-reviewer screening and an investigator-directed search are limitations.
